validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM. Southern Star Central Gas Pipeline, Inc. is a real, currently-operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission company (FERC company code 43) headquartered in Owensboro, KY, tracing to a 1904 predecessor and renamed several times (Cities Service Gas Co. 1926 -> Northwest Central Pipeline Corp. 1982 -> Williams Natural Gas Co. 1987 -> Williams Gas Pipeline Central 1997 -> Southern Star Central Gas Pipeline, Inc. 2003). Verified via Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org, article body/infobox, checked directly -- confirmed this is a company-type infobox, not auto-populated boilerplate) and, more importantly, via TWO 2026 government/trade sources showing the company actively filing with FERC: a Federal Register notice (2026-03-11) of a request under blanket authorization, and Pipeline & Gas Journal (2026-03-08) reporting FERC has opened environmental review of Southern Star's new 'Viola Project' (19.33 mi of 16-in Line UA in Sumner County, KS, connecting to existing 20-in Line U, to supply a 710-MW gas plant) -- this also confirms the company is actively expanding its system today, not a dormant/GEM-only entity. A FERC docket EA (CP19-31, 'ferc.gov/.../CP19-31-EA.pdf') for an earlier (2019-2020) project to abandon/replace Lines DT and DS was also read for background (via pdftotext -- the live URL's raw HTTP body doesn't extract cleanly through url_verifier's PDF handling, so it is NOT used as a citable ref here, but it independently confirms ongoing FERC-regulated construction activity under this same company name). CLASSIFICATION: correctly a natural gas transmission pipeline (GGIT gas tab) -- Wikipedia categorizes it under 'Natural gas pipelines in the United States' etc.; nothing suggests it should be reclassified. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 45-row Texas-operating roster -- no other row describes this system. Also checked a second, differently-named GEM wiki page that surfaced in search, 'gem.wiki/Southern_Star_Pipeline' -- that is a WHOLLY UNRELATED 14-mile CRUDE OIL connector (Jefferson Energy Vidor TX -> Motiva Port Neches TX, operator Jefferson Gulf Coast Energy Partners, started 2021, GOIT not GGIT). Confirmed NOT the same entity and NOT a duplicate/misfile -- the shared 'Southern Star' name is coincidental. HARVESTED CITATION POOL: this row's wiki page footnotes 5 sources; all 5 were opened this pass: (1) bit.ly/2sC090G resolves to the same Wikipedia article used below; (2) CDPQ press release -- verified live, supports ownership; (3) southernstar.com/about-us -- live domain but returns an access-block/challenge interstitial to automated fetches (kept per standing rule, not swapped/dropped, but not usable as a fresh citable ref this pass); (4) eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php -- reachable but is a generic data-directory/navigation page that does not itself name this pipeline or its values, so it is excluded as a navigation-surface citation (the egyptoil-gas.com lesson) rather than cited; (5) oilfieldwiki.com's page for this company -- the domain has been squatted and now serves unrelated pharmaceutical spam content ('Anavar For Sale'), i.e. the original citation is definitively gone, though not via a clean 404.

validity.recommendation: Consider reconciling StartLocation vs StartState -- no sheet edit forced this pass.
validity.researcher_notes: The Location cluster is flagged 'irregular' in the worklist, and rightly so: StartLocation='Rocky Mountains' paired with StartState/Province='Texas' is internally inconsistent taken literally (the Rocky Mountains are not in Texas). This is not a fabrication, though -- Wikipedia's own prose describes exactly this system: "Southern Star's Central Pipeline brings gas from the Rocky Mountains, Texas, and Oklahoma to Kansas. From there it goes east to Missouri." So StartLocation (Rocky Mountains), StartState (Texas), and EndState (Missouri) are each individually attested, but they describe THREE separate supply origins collapsed into one start-location field, which is why the region label and the state label don't match. A competing industry source (offshore-technology.com, GlobalData-syndicated) instead characterizes the pipeline as running Oklahoma -> Wyoming, which is a third, also-defensible reading of this same multi-directional trunk network. None of these is 'wrong' so much as GEM's single start/end schema being a poor fit for a >40-connection, 8-state distribution network. Recommend a human editor pick one consistent convention (e.g., StartLocation='Texas Panhandle/Hugoton area' with StartState='Texas', or generalize StartLocation to the network description) rather than leaving the Rockies/Texas mismatch as-is -- but I'm not overriding it unilaterally since all three components are independently sourced facts about the network, just inconsistently paired.

validity.recommendation: No sheet change -- documenting an ownership-layer nuance for the record only.
validity.researcher_notes: Owner1 = 'Southern Star Central Gas Pipeline Inc' at 100%, ref = southernstar.com/gis-maps/ (existing, access-blocked but correctly kept per standing rule). Worth flagging: the 2017 CDPQ press release (verified live) that GEM's own wiki page cites is titled 'La Caisse enters partnership to acquire Southern Star Central Corp' -- i.e. the transaction was for the PARENT holding company, 'Southern Star Central Corp', not directly for the pipeline-operating subsidiary listed as Owner1. Wikipedia's infobox separately lists 'Caisse de depot' as the company's Parent (with Ullico, Inc. as a co-investor per the CDPQ release). GEM's practice of recording the direct legal/operating entity as Owner1 is a defensible convention and I am not recommending a value change, but a future ownership-structure pass should record CDPQ/Ullico as the beneficial parent owners of Southern Star Central Corp, distinct from the pipeline-operating entity itself.

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent sources dated March 2026 (a Federal Register notice of Southern Star's own FERC blanket-authorization filing, and Pipeline & Gas Journal's report that FERC has opened environmental review of Southern Star's new Viola Project/Line UA in Kansas) both confirm the company is an active, currently-operating interstate gas pipeline as of this year -- not a historical or GEM-only entity.
Wikipedia describes it as a 'natural gas transmission system'; the Federal Register notice's own title names it a natural gas pipeline company. Both independent, both trivially corroborating.

Wikipedia's History section: 'The company was formed in 1904,' with the subsequent rename chain (1926/1982/1987/1997/2003) ending in the current name. Company-published sources (southernstar.com's own 'Southern Star celebrates 120 years of service' post, dated Aug 2024, i.e. 1904+120) independently corroborate the 1904 founding date but southernstar.com is access-blocked to automated verification (matches the existing block on this row's Owner ref), so it is not counted toward independence here -- tier held at medium (single verifiable source) rather than high.

Wikipedia's 'Pipeline statistics' table: 'System Design Capacity: 2.4 billion cubic feet ... per day' = 2,400 MMcf/d, exact match to the sheet. The company's own site states the same '2.4 Bcf/d' figure but is access-blocked to verification; offshore-technology.com's entry for this pipeline (industry database, independently verified live) covers length/diameter but not capacity, so a second verifiable independent source for the capacity figure specifically was not found this pass -- tier held at medium.

Wikipedia's statistics table gives 'Miles of Pipeline Approx 5,800' -- 5,800 mi x 1.60934 = 9,334.2 km, an EXACT match to the sheet's 9,334.00 km. offshore-technology.com (a separate, GlobalData-compiled industry database, independently verified live) puts it at 9,382 km, within 0.5% -- non-material rounding variance for a >5,000-mile trunk network, not a genuine spec conflict. (Note for the record, not actioned: Wikipedia's own INTRO paragraph, elsewhere on the same page, separately says 'approximately 6,000 miles (9,700 km)' and its infobox says 5,817 mi/9,362 km -- Wikipedia is internally inconsistent by a few percent across its own intro/infobox/statistics-table, and the sheet's figure lines up with the most granular of the three, the statistics table.)

Wikipedia directly attests each element: 'Southern Star's Central Pipeline brings gas from the Rocky Mountains, Texas, and Oklahoma to Kansas. From there it goes east to Missouri.' -- i.e. Rocky Mountains and Texas are both named supply origins, and Missouri is the eastern terminus, matching the sheet's StartLocation/StartState/EndState. See the paired validity finding (concern_type=attribution) for the caveat that StartLocation and StartState describe two DIFFERENT origins of the same multi-source network rather than one consistent start point, and that a competing source (offshore-technology.com) frames the network's direction differently (Oklahoma to Wyoming) -- both readings are defensible for a distribution network with 34+ connections across 8 states, so I have not proposed changing the values, only flagged the representation for a human call.

summary: P0253 Southern Star Central Gas Pipeline: existence, classification, and uniqueness all strongly confirmed (independent 2026 FERC/Federal Register/trade-press evidence of active operation, no duplicate against the roster or against the unrelated same-named oil connector); all 6 missing-ref units (Status/Fuel/Start/Capacity/Length/Location) sourced and staged as REFS_ADDED with no value changes; 3 caveat-level attribution/spec notes (StartLocation vs StartState mismatch on this network pipeline, Owner1=operating entity vs CDPQ/Ullico as ultimate parent, minor cross-source length variance ~9,334-9,700 km) documented but not auto-applied; Diameter left blank deliberately (network spans multiple diameters 16in-36in+ depending on segment, no single system-wide figure to source).
